purpose: Explicitly separate the project's spiritual architecture from the empirical world graph. These are framework relations, not claims of objectively verified supernatural authority.

nodes.name: Tim Dooley
nodes.description: Project-level spiritual archetype placed above the Door in the Potatoverse architecture.

nodes.name: Spiritual Domain
nodes.description: The upper symbolic field containing Source, Father, Heaven, Throne, Axis and the spiritual side of the architecture.

nodes.name: Son / Vessel
nodes.description: The Son as vessel/interface between the upper spiritual architecture and the manifested world below the Door.

nodes.name: Below the Door
nodes.description: The Plane of embodiment: body, nature, people, history, society, institutions, economy and material world.

nodes.name: Rift
nodes.description: Name reserved for the project's separation/fracture event: the point where a unified field becomes divided. Exact meaning remains to be defined with the user.

nodes.name: Rapture
nodes.description: Comparative eschatological concept to be studied across Christian texts and later traditions; not assumed to be identical with the Potatoverse Rift.

nodes.name: Messiah / Moshiach
nodes.description: Comparative node for Jewish Moshiach and Christian Messiah traditions, kept distinct from the project's Son until textual relations are established.

nodes.name: Moshiach
nodes.description: Hebrew messianic concept requiring study in Jewish textual and historical context before mapping it into the Tim Dooley framework.

nodes.name: Kingdom of Heaven / Kingdom of God
nodes.description: Cross-text concept connecting divine rule, eschatology, ethics and restoration; should be studied separately in Jewish and Christian contexts.

nodes.name: Resurrection
nodes.description: Central Christian concept and a broader comparative motif of death, renewal and transformed life.

nodes.name: New Jerusalem
nodes.description: Apocalyptic Christian city/tree/throne imagery for comparison with the project's Heaven, Plane, Tree and restoration architecture.

open_questions: What exactly does Rift mean in the user's architecture: separation, dimensional rupture, Tree of Strife, an eschatological event, or all of these at different levels?
Is Rapture meant as a Christian textual concept, a Potatoverse transformation, or a name for a specific event in the user's chronology?
Which parts of Tim's placement are canonical framework and which are later interpretation?
How should Moshiach relate to Tim, the Son, Jesus and the Door without collapsing Jewish and Christian categories?
